note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real in Git Bash scripts via 'bash'. The VPN gateway bills by the hour (about 4.5 EUR a day): tear down the same day. The Azure VPN Client profile and the Connect click are done by the owner.
prepare: # laptop toolchain for the bash scripts: Git Bash first on PATH, python3 and zip shims in %TEMP% (the laptop has neither)

$shim = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'mgshim'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $shim | Out-Null; [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\python3", "#!/bin/bash`nexec python `"`$@`"`n"); [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\zip.py", "import sys,os,zipfile`nz=zipfile.ZipFile(os.path.abspath(sys.argv[-2]),'w',zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)`n[z.write(os.path.join(r,n),os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r,n),'.').replace(os.sep,'/')) for r,d,f in os.walk('.') for n in f]`nz.close()`n"); [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\zip", "#!/bin/bash`nexec python `"`$(dirname `"`$0`")/zip.py`" `"`$@`"`n")
az account show --query name -o none 2>$null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { az login --use-device-code }   # owner signs in as labadmin
if (-not (Get-Command jq -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { winget install --id jqlang.jq -e --silent --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements }
# owner: install the Azure VPN Client from the Microsoft Store (once)
$pw = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'); [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PFX_PASSWORD', $pw, 'Process')   # random, process-only, never printed or stored
bash infra/certs.sh "$HOME/.contoso-net/certs" labadmin | Out-Null   # certificates made off camera so the password is never on screen; deploy.sh then skips this step

screens.name: netplan
screens.note: Runs anywhere. Expect one OK line (59 usable addresses, VM gets 10.61.0.4), then three ERROR lines.

screens.name: deploy
mask: gateway public IP and host name

steps: Open rg-mglab-azure-09: the gateway, public IP, two virtual networks and the VM
Open vgw-hub > Point-to-site configuration: pool 172.16.201.0/24, tunnel type IKEv2 and OpenVPN, authentication Azure certificate, root certificate contoso-p2s-root

screens.note: The wait is 45 minutes or more: record the real elapsed time in a caption and cut the wait in the edit, never fake it. Shows the plan OK line, certificates step (skipped), the what-if table (nine Create rows) and the start of the deployment.

screens.name: connect
commands: # now connect the 'contoso lab' profile in the Azure VPN Client
prepare: bash infra/vpnclient.sh rg-mglab-azure-09   # downloads the client package to ~/.contoso-net/client (run again after any peering or topology change)

# owner: Azure VPN Client > Add > Import the azurevpnconfig_cert.xml from $HOME\.contoso-net\client\unzipped\AzureVPN, name it 'contoso lab', pick the labadmin client certificate, Save. Leave it DISCONNECTED before the scene; click Connect during the pause
mask: gateway host name in the client window

steps: Show the profile 'contoso lab' with status Connected

screens.note: Expect first reachable false with a timeout and exit code 0, then after connecting reachable true, status 200, service contoso-orders-internal, host vm-orders-int and a client address from 172.16.201.0/24. If client differs or the probe times out, that is the finding (NSG source prefix; client package installed after the peering existed).

screens.name: diagnose
prepare: $env:VPN_CLIENT_IP = (python infra/probe.py 10.61.0.4 | ConvertFrom-Json).client   # the VPN must still be connected
screens.note: Show exactly what comes back, even if a next hop type differs from the comments in the script. The VM must be running. If it complains about Network Watcher: az network watcher configure -g NetworkWatcherRG -l westeurope --enabled true.

teardown: bash infra/teardown.sh rg-mglab-azure-09   # also deletes ~/.contoso-net (keys, pfx, client package)
# owner: delete the 'contoso lab' profile in the Azure VPN Client
az group exists --name rg-mglab-azure-09   # false when done
